name: Nucleosome core particle (1KX5, NCP147)
candidate_note: CANDIDATE only - not swapped into the viewer. Replacement needs Codex + Cursor (AGREE) and Kyrre approval (template v0.2 OQ2).
axes: right-handed; origin = DNA superhelix centre (revised 2026-10-08 16:18; same origin for all LODs), computed once from the 1KX5 atomic coordinates (see core_frame); +Y = DNA superhelical axis = least-variance principal axis of the DNA phosphorus atoms (unchanged), sign: H3 chain A on +Y side; +X = pseudo-dyad (unchanged; the dyad base pair lies 1.06° from +X, 0.005 nm from the X-Z plane); Z = X x Y.

organism.homolog_reason: histones are highly conserved; no C. elegans nucleosome structure in the catalog

species: Caenorhabditis elegans (target); structure Xenopus laevis histones + human DNA sequence

sources.citation: X-Ray Structure of the Nucleosome Core Particle, NCP147, at 1.9 A Resolution
sources.licence: CC0 1.0 (PDB archive data and RCSB APIs)

confidence_note: [VERIFY] confidence not set - to be decided by Codex/Cursor/Kyrre (models.py Evidence requires float 0-1)
instancing: one mesh per LOD; intended for heavy instancing along chromatin

build.L1: Gaussian density 20 Å / grid 4 Å, quadric decimation
build.L2: Gaussian density 10 Å (sigma 0.225*res) / grid 2.5 Å, iso-level enclosing mass x 1.21 Å^3/Da, marching cubes, quadric decimation
build.validation: Khronos glTF-Validator: 0 errors, 0 warnings (all LODs incl. anchor)
build.core_frame_fix: organeller-shared/tools/fix_mol0012_core_frame.py --build (L1/L2/L3 rebuilt with the superhelix-centre origin); dedup/prune; validator 0 errors/0 warnings

asset.note: Decided by Kyrre 2026-10-07: All rights reserved (© Kyrre Grøtan) until further notice (keeps commercialisation open); a possible open release (e.g. CC BY-NC) may come later. Applies to our own 3D assets/manifests only; every source keeps its own licence and attribution.

wwPDB/RCSB PDB.licence: CC0 1.0 (PDB archive data and RCSB APIs)

license.summary: All inputs CC0 / CC BY (commercial use allowed); no NC/academic-only source. Own asset: All rights reserved (© Kyrre Grøtan).

core_frame.method: DNA superhelix centre from 1KX5 C1' base-pair centres (author chains I/J = label A/B), circle fit in the X-Z plane of the unchanged rotation; Y = mean bp-centre Y

source.model: model 1 = asymmetric unit = biological assembly 1 (one NCP)

core_frame.chain_id_convention: DNA = author chains I/J (= label A/B); histones = author A-H. Never treat author A/B as DNA.
core_frame.pairing: author I residue i <-> author J residue -i (1KX5 numbering -73..73; dyad = i 0)
core_frame.old_origin: bbox centre of all atoms in the rotated frame (tail-driven); old origin lies at old_origin_in_new_frame_nm
core_frame.lod_check: new L1/L2/L3 vertices = old vertices + old_origin_in_new_frame_nm (pure translation, max deviation 0.0004 nm = rounding) - one common transform for all LODs
core_frame.note_axis: [VERIFY for reviewers] a free cylinder fit to the bp centres gives an axis 12.1° from the kept +Y (tilted about X; 89.6° to the dyad). The origin lies 0.044 nm from that fitted axis, so the centre does not depend on the choice. The rotation was kept unchanged as instructed; changing +Y to the cylinder axis would be a separate, reviewable change.

learner_text: Xenopus histones / human DNA sequence stand-in (PDB 1KX5); illustrative proxy for the C. elegans nucleosome.

target_equivalents.note: C. elegans equivalents, NOT replacements (multigene histone families; one representative accession per histone). verified via UniProt REST 2026-10-08 (gene names and ORFs; WBGene IDs not re-checked here).
